name: Shadrach/Hananiah
title: The Tried Servant
summary: Hananiah was one of the four young Hebrews taken to Babylon during Nebuchadnezzar's first deportation. He received the Babylonian name Shadrach and is best known for his unwavering faith when, together with his friends, he refused to worship the golden statue and was thrown into the fiery furnace, yet miraculously saved by God.

keyEvents.title: The Deportation to Babylon
keyEvents.description: Hananiah was among the young Israelites of royal lineage chosen to serve at Nebuchadnezzar's court.

keyEvents.title: Name Change
keyEvents.description: Hananiah received the Babylonian name Shadrach from the chief official as part of their assimilation into Babylonian culture.

keyEvents.title: The Dietary Protest
keyEvents.description: Together with Daniel and the others, Hananiah refused to eat food from the king's table and stuck to vegetables and water to follow God's law.

keyEvents.title: Appointment as an official
keyEvents.description: After Daniel interpreted Nebuchadnezzar's dream, Shadrach was appointed to govern the province of Babylon together with Meshach and Abednego.

keyEvents.title: Refusal to worship the golden statue
keyEvents.description: When Nebuchadnezzar ordered everyone to worship the golden statue he had set up, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refused to bow down, despite the threat of death.

keyEvents.title: Deliverance from the fiery furnace
keyEvents.description: The three were thrown into the blazing furnace, but God sent his angel to protect them. They came out unharmed, and the king praised their God.
